card: This pull request bumps the minimum required C++ standard from C++20 to C++23, raising compiler requirements to GCC 13 and Clang 19. It removes internal polyfills like util::Expected and custom byteswap routines in favor of std::expected and std::byteswap, and mechanically converts string search calls to std::string::contains. The author notes that workarounds to avoid C++23 are accumulating and that dependencies like libmultiprocess already use C++23 features, though incomplete standard library support in some compilers remains a consideration. It is marked as an RFC/WIP nomerge discussion PR and unblocks work tracked in #34979.
changed_since_previous: Added use of std::views::zip in btck block imports, addressed include-what-you-use (IWYU) headers, and refined util::Expected test cases for C++23 semantics.
evidence: Author description: "the workarounds to avoid C++23 keep accumulating and some parts of the code already use C++23 features, such as lambda attributes (https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/commit/bdd0cd69418d189f62699d274a751cbf6d36bb43)."
Author notes the compiler baseline increase: "GCC: 13, Clang: 19" while noting some standard library features like <stacktrace> and ranges::starts_with are still not uniformly available.
problem: Bitcoin Core is currently restricted to C++20, forcing developers to maintain custom polyfills and workarounds (such as util::Expected, byte swapping functions, and ALWAYS_FALSE templates) even as adjacent subprojects like libmultiprocess already use C++23 features.

risk.why: Bumping compiler standard and minimum toolchain versions affects release binaries across all supported platforms and risks subtle toolchain or standard library bugs across the entire codebase.

scope_notes: Marked RFC and nomerge by the author. Includes large mechanical conversions of .find(...) != npos to .contains(...) across over 50 files, alongside deleting util::Expected tests in favor of standard library std::expected.
summary: This pull request raises the required C++ standard to C++23 across CMake, depends, and CI, bumping minimum compiler toolchains to GCC 13 and Clang 19. It replaces Bitcoin Core's internal polyfills with standard library equivalents, migrating util::Expected to std::expected and custom byteswap routines to std::byteswap. Additionally, it adopts std::views::zip, removes obsolete template workarounds like ALWAYS_FALSE, and converts substring checks across the codebase to std::string::contains.
